item.title: How to Get a 100% Quality Dress in Dressmaker
item.description:
Making a dress that meets your customer's requirements is only half the job in Dressmaker . If you want to get 100% quality and the 99 Problems But a Stitch Ain't One achievement, you need to be careful with every step. Even a small mistake can bring the score down, so it's easy to end up with a dress that's almost perfect but not quite there. Here's what you need to do to get the 100% perfect quality dress in Dressmaker .

10 Cozy Video Games That Are Perfect for the Holiday Season

The holidays are the perfect time to shift gears and enjoy these cozy games with stress-free gameplay.

By Anastasia Maillot

How to Get 100% Quality in Dressmaker

There are three things you need to get right if you want a perfect dress:

  • Measurements
  • Grain quality
  • Sew lines.

The whole process starts with measurements. After a customer explains her requirements, you take her measurements. First, take their sizes, then make sure that the mannequin matches those measurements perfectly.

You can see the measurements while you adjust the mannequin, so take a look to ensure you get the perfect measurements!

Next up is Grain Quality. When you place the pattern pieces on the fabric, you can see a percentage on the screen. The direction of each piece affects its grain quality , so make sure to position them correctly. You will see its percentage as you move the pieces. For a perfect dress, you want a 100% grain quality.

Lastly, you need to be careful while sewing. Take your time around the edges and try to follow the lines as closely as possible. It can take some time, but it's much easier to keep your quality high this way.

If you are having trouble, you can also turn on Sewing Assist from the settings to make things a little easier.

The good thing is that the indie game shows your current quality at each step. When taking measurements, you will see the measurements you need to match. You will also see the percentage while moving the pattern pieces and sewing the dress.

item.title: Steam Users Can Claim 10/10 Masterpiece for Free, Plus 7 More Free Games
item.description:
Steam users can currently claim free Keys for 8 games (including a 10/10 masterpiece and a handful of other titles), as long as they claim them before November 2 . Steam users have a full month to do so, obviously, but time flies when free PC games are waiting to be claimed. In other words, Steam users should be sure to pick up these titles before they no longer have the option.

It's worth noting that, for these specific games, Steam users will need a membership with Humble Bundle for access to the free Humble Choice games. The first Tuesday of every month, Humble rotates a selection of free games as an added benefit to the core paid features, ranging from access to the Humble Vault and Special Membership deals to charity contributions. In general, it's a solid way for gamers to save money every month and still get plenty of games to play, alongside the paid expanded access to Humble.

New RPG Like Hi-Fi-Rush on Steam Is Already a Massive Hit

Steam has a new rhythm-driven RPG that could appeal to Hi-Fi Rush fans, and early players are responding extremely well to it.

By Adrian Morales

Free Humble Choice Game List for October 2026

  • Check Out the Humble Choice Free Games for October 2026
    • Available until November 2 at 10 am PT/1 pm ET
    • Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii
    • Psychonauts 2
    • Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown
    • Deep Rock Galactic: Survivor
    • Cataclismo
    • Dungeons and Degenerate Gambles
    • Asgard's Fall: Viking Survivors
    • Toy Shire

Headlining the Humble Choice Games for October 2026 is a trio of games: Psychonauts 2, Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown , and Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii, a fitting follow-up to when Humble Choice gave out Steam Keys of Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth for free in August 2026. This spin-off title gives Goro Majima a pirate adventure in Hawaii and leans heavily into the zaniness of the franchise. Beyond that, fans can pick up Deep Rock Galactic: Survivor, Cataclismo, Dungeons and Degenerate Gamblers, Asgard's Fall: Viking Survivors , and Toy Shire .

Find the odd one out before the timer hits zero.

Round 1

Psychonauts 2 is a fantastic 10/10 platform-adventure game masterpiece from 2021, picking up the franchise after a decade+ wait. Its Steam Key alone justifies membership, well beyond its core values, and it's joined by several other great games. It's worth noting that this timing may or may not be a coincidence, as Double Fine Productions works to stabilize after stepping away from its status as an Xbox studio. Overall, if someone hasn't played Psychonauts or a Double Fine game, it's impossible to go wrong with Psychonauts 2.

Meanwhile, Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown balances out the zaniness of Like a Dragon with the more humorous gameplay of Psychonauts 2 . It's an instant classic Metroidvania game and easily one of the best Ubisoft games in recent years, so this trio alone is hard to pass up.

Humble Choice Free Games for October 2026 Explained

  • Deep Rock Galactic: Survivor - A single-player survivor-like spin-off of Deep Rock Galactic , this game has players controlling a lone dwarf while fighting through massive swarms of hostile aliens. Players mine valuable resources, upgrade their weapons and equipment, and push deeper into increasingly dangerous caves.
  • Cataclismo - A real-time strategy and tower-defense game set in a dark fantasy world devastated by a mysterious cataclysm. Players gather resources, construct fortified settlements piece by piece, and defend their survivors from relentless hordes of monsters.
  • Dungeons and Degenerate Gamblers - A deck-building roguelike game that combines traditional card mechanics with dungeon-crawling adventure gameplay. Players build increasingly powerful decks, battle enemies, and take risky gambles as they attempt to survive each run.
  • Asgard's Fall: Viking Survivors - A fast-paced survivor-like action game inspired by Norse mythology, putting players in control of a warrior battling through hordes of enemies. Players control a Viking warrior, collect upgrades and weapons, and fight through waves of enemies while attempting to survive each run.
  • Toy Shire - A charming tower-defense game where players defend a miniature toy kingdom from waves of enemies. Players build and upgrade defenses across colorful diorama-like environments while using different toys and strategic combinations to hold the line.

item.title: Xbox Game Pass Is Losing One of This Century's Greatest RPGs, But It Doesn't Need It Anymore Anyway
item.description:
Contrary to popular belief, the best marketing strategy can sometimes be just letting people play your game for free. It may sound counterproductive, but subscription services like Xbox Game Pass have proved this strategy to be successful over and over again. Spending money on an unfamiliar IP seems to be way less likely than clicking the download button on a game that's already included in a subscription anyway; it just eliminates a lot of the mental gymnastics that usually come with spending money.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is one of the best examples of how much accessibility changes the rules. Creative director Guillaume Broche has said that Game Pass significantly lowered the barrier for people who might otherwise hesitate to try a turn-based RPG, and Microsoft later confirmed that Expedition 33 became its biggest new third-party Game Pass launch of 2025. However, now that Game Pass has already done its job, those who are now hooked on the game may be perfectly willing to buy it after it leaves the service.

This GOTY Contender is Xbox Game Pass' Biggest Third-Party Title of the Year

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is the biggest third-party game launch on Xbox Game Pass in 2025, surpassing all other titles in its first 30 days.

2
By Anthony Taormina

Game Pass Has Done Its Job and It Has Done It Well

Arguably, Game Pass was most valuable to Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 when people still had no idea whether they would like it or not. Like every new game, this one had some convincing to do, especially since its turn-based combat was already acting as a barrier for players who prefer RPGs with real-time combat. Game Pass quickly removed that barrier by making Expedition 33 considerably easier to try without much thought. It was like one of those old habit-building tricks: if you don't drink enough water during the day, simply scatter bottles around your house where you'll see them often. Sooner or later, the constant exposure will make you shrug and take a sip every time you look at one.

Of course, this marketing strategy only works if what you are selling is actually valuable, and Expedition 33 has done a pretty good job of making its case. Sandfall Interactive announced that the RPG had sold 5 million copies only five months after its release, which means that its success was not even limited to Game Pass subscribers. The game also received widespread recognition at major award shows, which gave people who had never heard of it before plenty of reasons to get familiar with it. Game Pass may have been extremely important when Sandfall still had to convince people the game was good, but those days are over; Expedition 33 's reputation is now capable of carrying the game on its own.

Game Pass availability can vary by region and subscription tier.

Leaving Game Pass Could Be Clair Obscur's Next Big Test

Ironically, giving people free stuff is often exactly what converts them into buyers. Anyone who started playing Clair Obscure: Expedition 33 through their subscription and still has unfinished business after it disappears will suddenly have two very straightforward options: either stop playing or buy the game. After Game Pass made people's first interaction with the title so easy, now players have something much more valuable than a short trailer to rely on when it comes to making their decision — their own experience. While buying an unfamiliar IP is a gamble, purchasing a game you know is good is a completely different story.

This also highlights what Expedition 33 achieved beyond generating a large number of players at launch. It actually helped the game reach people who were never necessarily fans of the genre in the first place. Although it might have been easy to convince turn-based RPG fans to give it a shot, the same cannot be said for everyone else; if it hadn't been for the Game Pass strategy, Expedition 33 probably wouldn't have reached many of the people who are now hooked on the game. Additionally, now that the title has already won over some real-time combat lovers, leaving Game Pass would not suddenly erase the interest it managed to build among them.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Played the Long Game

It would make sense that getting millions of people at launch means considerably less if most of them turn around and leave after the first 30 days. Player retention has become one of the most important metrics across the gaming industry, as long-term value naturally matters more in a world where more than 20,000 games launch on Steam alone in a single year.

Xbox Game Pass Is Losing One of This Century's Greatest RPGs, But It Doesn't Need It Anymore Anyway
Ex-PlayStation Boss Shawn Layden Tells Xbox CEO Asha Sharma to "Pick a Lane"
Gears of War: E-Day is Already Breaking Records
10 Best Games on Xbox Game Pass (October 2026)

Expedition 33 had the benefit of Game Pass, which made the initial discovery of the RPG game incredibly easy, but getting people to download the game was only the first half of the job; the more important part was giving them enough reason to remain invested once the novelty wore off. In that sense, Expedition 33 is a good reminder that making a great game and selling it are two very different jobs. Additionally, making less money at the beginning is exactly what might bring them a fortune later, ultimately proving that sometimes less really is more. For Clair Obscur , at least, things might have fallen into place pretty nicely.

item.title: After 13 Years, GTA 6's Jason Is Leaning on One of GTA 5's Most Important Strengths
item.description:
If Grand Theft Auto were all about surrounding its protagonists with good people, we wouldn't have half of the characters that made the franchise so memorable. Criminals and weirdos have always been a big part of the series, and GTA 5 is a title that made particularly good use of them. The previous entry had three protagonists, each with their own social circle, and it's safe to say that none of them were exactly surrounded by angels. However, they were also a big part of what made crime feel so natural in the protagonists' world.

It appears that thirteen years later, Grand Theft Auto 6 is ready to lean into this same formula when it comes to Jason. According to Rockstar, GTA 6's Jason did not grow up in the best environment, and the people currently surrounding him certainly suggest that not much has changed. Brian Heder and Cal Hampton are great examples of what Jason considers to be normal company, but neither sounds like someone who is about to steer him away from trouble. Of course, this is not necessarily a bad thing, especially considering how well the same premise worked for GTA 5 .

10 Details You Probably Missed in the GTA 6 Extended Look

GTA 6’s Extended Look was packed with small details, hidden mechanics, and easy-to-miss moments that reveal even more about Leonida.

By Josh Cotts

GTA 6 Is Skipping a Few Steps With Jason

Jason might be living his best life when it comes to his living arrangement—or so it seems. He doesn't have to worry about rent prices going up because Brian Heder, his landlord, is a veteran drug runner who couldn't care less about Jason's money. He has been smuggling drugs through the Keys for years and still moves product through his boatyard with his third wife, Lori. Of course, being so far along in his career means that he doesn't usually handle the dirty work himself. That's what people like Jason are for. The protagonist may be allowed to live in his apartment rent-free, but he needs to make sure he holds up his end of the deal by helping Brian with local shakedowns.

This arrangement shows that Jason isn't being suddenly pulled into the world of crime at the start of GTA 6 . After all, one probably needs to be pretty comfortable with that lifestyle already to agree to live under a criminal's roof. This approach is hardly new for the franchise, as GTA 5 's protagonists were already heavily involved in the world of crime, too. That way, the game is free to focus on how to develop the narrative moving forward and help players reach the meat of the story much faster.

Having a Normal Life Was Never Really an Option for Jason

Speaking of Brian Heder, it's hard not to think of another associate of his: Cal Hampton. He spends his time drinking beers and snooping on Coast Guard communications while simultaneously being chronically concerned about birds flying in suspiciously perfect formations. While Brian may be the character who represents the criminal side of Jason's life, Cal seems to have the weirdness aspect covered. Rockstar describes Cal as perfectly happy with the way his life is going.

On the other hand, there's Jason with his allegedly huge plans. Although they seem too different from each other, this is the type of friendship that often lasts in real life. Story-wise, maybe the purpose of this friendship is to show players how easily Jason could choose to just relax, have a beer, and chill with his questionable friends. However, Jason clearly has something bigger in mind, even if Rockstar Games is still keeping the details to itself.

GTA 5 May Have Left GTA 6 a Useful Blueprint

The truth is that neither Brian nor Cal sounds like the best person to call in an emergency. However, GTA 5 has proven that surrounding the protagonist with characters like them is one of the best strategies to make this world as believable and as immersive as possible. Franklin had Lamar pulling him toward bad ideas, while Trevor's social circle included characters such as the conspiracy-minded Ron and the strange but loyal Wade. Moreover, most people will probably agree that it's exactly these characters who bring humor into the otherwise pretty serious business of being a criminal.

GTA 6 is currently scheduled to release on November 19, 2026, for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

In any case, Brian and Cal's purpose probably isn't to copy GTA 5 , but they establish a good baseline of what Jason's life looks like before his life becomes more complicated. Moreover, just like in real life, one's friends can tell us a lot about a person, and Jason's relationship with both Cal and Brian gives Rockstar a whole new way to define him. Without a doubt, GTA 5 benefited from the same thing as well; for example, Franklin's relationship with Lamar reveals a side of him that players would have never been able to see just from the missions with Michael. And if GTA 6 's aim was to copy that same approach, then Jason's relationships could end up doing a lot more of the heavy lifting than people imagine.

GTA 6’s Extended Look was packed with small details, hidden mechanics, and easy-to-miss moments that reveal even more about Leonida.

By Josh Cotts

GTA 6 Is Skipping a Few Steps With Jason

Jason might be living his best life when it comes to his living arrangement—or so it seems. He doesn't have to worry about rent prices going up because Brian Heder, his landlord, is a veteran drug runner who couldn't care less about Jason's money. He has been smuggling drugs through the Keys for years and still moves product through his boatyard with his third wife, Lori. Of course, being so far along in his career means that he doesn't usually handle the dirty work himself. That's what people like Jason are for. The protagonist may be allowed to live in his apartment rent-free, but he needs to make sure he holds up his end of the deal by helping Brian with local shakedowns.

This arrangement shows that Jason isn't being suddenly pulled into the world of crime at the start of GTA 6 . After all, one probably needs to be pretty comfortable with that lifestyle already to agree to live under a criminal's roof. This approach is hardly new for the franchise, as GTA 5 's protagonists were already heavily involved in the world of crime, too. That way, the game is free to focus on how to develop the narrative moving forward and help players reach the meat of the story much faster.

Having a Normal Life Was Never Really an Option for Jason

Speaking of Brian Heder, it's hard not to think of another associate of his: Cal Hampton. He spends his time drinking beers and snooping on Coast Guard communications while simultaneously being chronically concerned about birds flying in suspiciously perfect formations. While Brian may be the character who represents the criminal side of Jason's life, Cal seems to have the weirdness aspect covered. Rockstar describes Cal as perfectly happy with the way his life is going.

On the other hand, there's Jason with his allegedly huge plans. Although they seem too different from each other, this is the type of friendship that often lasts in real life. Story-wise, maybe the purpose of this friendship is to show players how easily Jason could choose to just relax, have a beer, and chill with his questionable friends. However, Jason clearly has something bigger in mind, even if Rockstar Games is still keeping the details to itself.

GTA 5 May Have Left GTA 6 a Useful Blueprint

The truth is that neither Brian nor Cal sounds like the best person to call in an emergency. However, GTA 5 has proven that surrounding the protagonist with characters like them is one of the best strategies to make this world as believable and as immersive as possible. Franklin had Lamar pulling him toward bad ideas, while Trevor's social circle included characters such as the conspiracy-minded Ron and the strange but loyal Wade. Moreover, most people will probably agree that it's exactly these characters who bring humor into the otherwise pretty serious business of being a criminal.

GTA 6 is currently scheduled to release on November 19, 2026, for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

In any case, Brian and Cal's purpose probably isn't to copy GTA 5 , but they establish a good baseline of what Jason's life looks like before his life becomes more complicated. Moreover, just like in real life, one's friends can tell us a lot about a person, and Jason's relationship with both Cal and Brian gives Rockstar a whole new way to define him. Without a doubt, GTA 5 benefited from the same thing as well; for example, Franklin's relationship with Lamar reveals a side of him that players would have never been able to see just from the missions with Michael. And if GTA 6 's aim was to copy that same approach, then Jason's relationships could end up doing a lot more of the heavy lifting than people imagine.

item.title: CEO Asha Sharma Comments on Next-Gen Xbox Helix Consoles
item.description:
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has reportedly vowed that Project Helix will be a "great console," but also not the be-all and end-all of Microsoft's next-gen hardware plans. While her comments were largely aimed at reassuring employees that the company's embattled gaming vision isn't going anywhere, they also provided a clearer picture of how exactly the next-gen Xbox console lineup will look.

Microsoft formally detailed Project Helix earlier in 2026, describing its Series X/S successor as a custom AMD-powered system designed to play both Xbox console and PC games. The tech giant plans to begin shipping alpha units to developers sometime in 2027, with company officials outright saying as much on several occasions. However, Microsoft has yet to indicate a Project Helix release window, let alone commit to one.

Asha Sharma Issues Statement on Xbox Sale Rumors

Following months of speculation, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma responds to rumors that Microsoft is looking to offload its embattled gaming division.

By Dominik Bošnjak

Xbox Helix Won't Be a Console, But a Whole Device Lineup

Sharma Reiterates High-Level Plans While Revealing Some New Info About Next-Gen Xbox

Sharma recently offered some additional clues about Microsoft's plans to employees, Windows Central reports, citing a transcript of an internal Xbox town hall from early October 2026. During the gathering, the executive is said to have described "Gen-10" as a "family of devices," stressing that Microsoft will "certainly have a great console first" while pursuing a more comprehensive hardware strategy designed to cater to a broad audience. Elaborating on the reasons for that approach, Sharma reportedly said there is "not one device that fits all," acknowledging that no matter how capable the company's upcoming home console proves to be, some players will simply have no interest in it. "Many players will be on the go," she said, referring to the growing handheld gaming market, as per the same transcript.

Next Xbox Console Family Will Seemingly Include a Handheld

Possibly a Direct Successor to Xbox Series S

Another noteworthy detail from the leak is the suggestion that Microsoft intends to outsource at least some of its next-generation gaming hardware. "There are some things that we are the best in the world to manufacture, and there are other things that we will partner on," the transcript reads, effectively confirming that at least one device in the Xbox Helix generation will be produced in partnership with another company. A handheld appears to be the most obvious candidate for that still-unannounced device, not least because it was only a year ago that Microsoft had partnered with ASUS on the ROG Xbox Ally and Ally X. The 2025 handheld PCs were officially framed as a result of the same train of thought: Xbox did not have handheld expertise, but ASUS did.

The fact that Project Helix will include more than one device is not entirely new, though it was only recently confirmed. Sharma first used the "family of devices" wording in a late August 2026 interview with the BBC, albeit without delving into the finer details she reportedly shared during the early October town hall. Regardless, many questions about Microsoft's post-Series X/S console lineup remain unanswered. Previous reporting citing industry insiders has raised the possibility that Project Helix could support third-party storefronts well beyond just the Xbox Store. Another major uncertainty is whether Microsoft's future hardware will continue to support physical games.

At Least Some Xbox Helix Models May Support Physical Games

Gears of War E-Day Is Being Review Bombed
Xbox Game Pass Is Losing One of This Century's Greatest RPGs, But It Doesn't Need It Anymore Anyway
After 13 Years, GTA 6's Jason Is Leaning on One of GTA 5's Most Important Strengths
CEO Asha Sharma Comments on Next-Gen Xbox Helix Consoles

Sony is still facing pressure and backlash from vocal consumers over its decision to stop manufacturing physical copies of new PlayStation games released from 2028 onward, meaning a different approach on this front could give Microsoft an opportunity to win back some goodwill. The recently expanded Xbox Disc-to-Digital program suggests that preserving access to existing physical libraries remains part of the company's broader ecosystem strategy, but it offers no indication that any Xbox Helix device will actually ship with a disc drive or cartridge slot. One possible middle ground would be to launch a digital-only console, but while making it modular and selling an optional disc reader separately. Microsoft has already tried the former approach, but only Sony paired it with the latter.
